# Session Persistence & Resume

Covers how Claude Code stores, resumes, forks, and manages conversation sessions.

## Session Storage

Conversations are saved locally as plaintext JSONL files under `~/.claude/projects/` [12]. Each message, tool use, and result is written to the file, enabling rewinding, resuming, and forking sessions [12]. Session persistence is enabled by default and requires no explicit activation [20].

## Resume and Continue

| Command | Behavior |
|---------|----------|
| `claude --continue` / `claude -c` | Load most recent conversation in current directory [4] |
| `claude --resume` / `claude -r` | Interactive picker to choose a session [4] |
| `claude --resume <id-or-name>` | Resume specific session by ID or display name [4] |
| `claude -c -p "query"` | Continue most recent session in SDK/print mode [4] |

When resuming, full conversation history is restored, but session-scoped permissions are NOT restored — those must be re-approved [12].

## Session Naming and Search

- `--name` / `-n`: Set display name for session, shown in `/resume` and terminal title [4]
- `/rename`: Change name mid-session [4]
- `claude --resume <name>`: Resume by display name [4]
- The `/resume` picker shows sessions from the current worktree by default, with keyboard shortcuts to widen to other worktrees or projects [12]

## Forking Sessions

`--fork-session`: Creates a new session ID while preserving conversation history up to that point [4][12]. The original session remains unchanged. Useful for branching off to try different approaches without affecting the original [12].

```bash
claude --continue --fork-session
```

Same session resumed in multiple terminals: both write to the same file, messages interleave. Nothing corrupts, but conversation becomes jumbled. Use `--fork-session` for parallel work from the same starting point [12].

## PR-Linked Sessions

`--from-pr`: Resume sessions linked to a pull request number or URL. Sessions are linked automatically when Claude creates the PR [4]. Accepts GitHub, GitHub Enterprise, GitLab, and Bitbucket URLs [4].

## Checkpointing and /rewind

Every user prompt creates a checkpoint before file edits [11]. Checkpoints persist across sessions and are cleaned up after 30 days (configurable) [11].

### Rewind Actions

Access via Esc+Esc or `/rewind` command [11]:

| Action | Effect |
|--------|--------|
| Restore code and conversation | Revert both to selected point |
| Restore conversation | Rewind to message, keep current code |
| Restore code | Revert file changes, keep conversation |
| Summarize from here | Compress from selected point forward |
| Never mind | Return without changes |

After restore, the original prompt from the selected message is restored into the input field [11].

### Summarize vs Restore

Summarize differs from restore [11]:
- Messages before selection stay intact
- Selected + subsequent messages replaced with AI-generated summary
- No files on disk are changed
- Original messages preserved in transcript
- Like `/compact` but targeted: keep early context, compress later parts

### Checkpoint Limitations

- Bash command changes (rm, mv, cp) NOT tracked [11]
- External/manual changes NOT tracked [11]
- Only tracks files edited through Claude's file editing tools [11]
- Not a replacement for version control [11]

## Headless/Print Mode (-p)

Previously called "headless mode," now accessed via `-p` flag [10]:

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `-p` / `--print` | Non-interactive, print response and exit [10] |
| `--bare` | Skip auto-discovery of hooks, skills, plugins, MCP, auto memory, CLAUDE.md [10] |
| `--no-session-persistence` | Disable saving sessions to disk (print mode only) [10] |
| `--output-format` | text, json, stream-json [10] |
| `--max-turns` | Limit agentic turns [10] |
| `--max-budget-usd` | Spending limit [10] |

`--bare` is recommended for scripted/SDK calls and will become default for `-p` in a future release [10].

## /clear Command

`/clear` starts a fresh context in the current directory [17]. Use when beginning genuinely new tasks — provides zero context rot since you control exactly which information carries forward [17].

## Worktree Isolation

`--worktree` / `-w`: Start Claude in an isolated git worktree at `<repo>/.claude/worktrees/<name>` [4]. Combined with `--tmux` to launch in a tmux session [4].

Subagents can also use worktree isolation via `isolation: "worktree"` in Agent tool parameters [9].

Each worktree gets its own working directory, so parallel Claude Code sessions cannot conflict [12].

## Session Independence

Each new session starts with a fresh context window without conversation history from previous sessions [12]. Two mechanisms carry knowledge across sessions:
1. Auto memory: notes Claude writes based on corrections/preferences [8]
2. CLAUDE.md: instructions you write for persistent context [8]

## Gaps and Limitations

- Session-scoped permissions are not restored on resume [12]
- No built-in session search beyond the picker (community tool `raine/claude-history` provides fuzzy search) [discovery agent findings]
- Sessions created by `claude -p` do not appear in picker but can be resumed by ID [discovery agent findings]
- GitHub issue #43696 reports potential context restoration failures with --continue/--resume [discovery agent findings]
